A financial crisis that began in Thailand in July 1997 and spread across East and Southeast Asia. On the chart this item marks its effect on South Korea; the Southeast Asian side has its own entry.

Fast growing economies had borrowed heavily in dollars for short terms. When Thailand let the baht float, investors pulled money out of Indonesia, Malaysia and South Korea too. Currencies and stock markets fell sharply.

In South Korea several large chaebol, the family run conglomerates, collapsed under their debts. In December 1997 the country took a rescue package of about 57 billion dollars from the International Monetary Fund, at the time the largest ever. Koreans call it the IMF crisis. Millions queued to donate gold to help pay the debt. The new president, Kim Dae-jung, closed weak banks and forced the chaebol to cut debt; Daewoo broke up in 1999.

Korea recovered quickly. In Indonesia the crisis brought the fall of Suharto.
